scoring_justification: Transition temperatures cannot be recomputed from submitted raw data (only self-reported numbers), so T0 compare to paper-reported values is used. Specific heat and defect density are checked structurally (peak location, single peak, steepest increase) and against hidden paper references from the raw CSV data.

hidden_assets.purpose: Hidden gold reference values for simulation transition temperatures and specific heat peak from the paper.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text: solid-hexatic gamma_m_sim=69.25, hexatic-isotropic gamma_i_sim=68.25, specific heat peak at 68.5 (from simulation results).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the published paper (PRL 113, 127801) and used as hidden reference for result-level comparison.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values are directly quoted from the paper's simulation results and used as gold standard for reproduction evaluation.

outputs.description: Solid–hexatic and hexatic–isotropic inverse transition temperatures Γ_m and Γ_i determined from the decay of the orientational correlation function g₆(r).
Specific heat per particle c_N as a function of inverse temperature Γ, computed from energy fluctuations in the MC simulations.

Defect densities (total, isolated dislocations, isolated disclinations) as a function of Γ. The checker will verify that the steepest increase in isolated dislocations coincides with the specific heat peak.

output_contract.notes: The MC simulation must sweep a sufficient range of Γ (covering solid, hexatic, isotropic) to reliably determine the transition points and resolve the specific heat peak. The specific heat peak is expected to lie inside the hexatic phase (Γ_i < Γ_peak < Γ_m).
